# incomplete fixtures

Half-typed input. For each `*.rsx` the parser must return an AST with error nodes (never panic), and recovery-mode codegen must emit Rust in which every complete Rust expression is still analyzable by rust-analyzer. These three are required for Gate 1.

Each `*.rsx` also has a sibling `*.expected` listing the Outou diagnostics it must produce, verbatim and in the order the parser emits them (innermost construct first), in the same format as `tests/fixtures/diagnostics/`. Rust-level errors from blocks the parser closes implicitly at end of input are not listed, except for an unclosed function body cut at the next item, which is always listed (``unclosed body of function …``, `docs/grammar.md` §9). These files are whole mid-edit buffers: a trailing `}` that closes the enclosing `fn` is part of what recovery must handle (`docs/grammar.md` §2.2).

The `*-mid-file` fixtures (a `fn Before` above, a `fn After` below; `bodyless-fn-mid-file`, `class-attribute-value-mid-file`, `unclosed-island-mid-file`, `unclosed-tag-mid-file`) also pin the swallowed-tail fix: `fn After` must survive as its own item (`swallowed_tail_fixtures_keep_the_item_after_the_broken_construct` in `crates/outou-backend-dioxus/tests/recovery.rs`). `fragment-truncated-closing-tag-eof` (a truncated `</` right after a reserved `<>`) and `stray-truncated-closing-tag-eof` (a top-level `</div` at end of file) are the `recover_fragment` / `recover_stray_close` regressions. The `stray-closing-tag-interrupted-by-{rbrace,lt}` and `fragment-closing-tag-interrupted-by-{rbrace,lt}` fixtures pin the `}`- and `<`-interrupted shapes of the same two recoveries (a `<` that starts JSX is consumed into the recovery element so Recovery output stays valid Rust).
